That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most

  Candidate directions:

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

memory_block.body: Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition; note when citing it.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

answer.rationale:
The loudest signal is the competitor's entry pricing, which pulls toward promotional_pricing — but that is exactly the direction whose inherited support is weakest and most costly if wrong. memory_73 carries an explicit caveat: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of cohort mixing rather than a real effect. Discount-led acquisition also has the worst downstream profile against the stated objective: it buys price-motivated accounts that dilute margin, anchor expectations low, and tend to churn or resist expansion, so short-term revenue lift can subtract from sustainable qualified revenue. I therefore spend one verification pull on memory_73 to see whether the effect survives de-pooling, so I am declining it on evidence rather than on reflex.

The internal signals point elsewhere and are self-consistent: onboarding completion down 4% and activation down 6% look like one funnel problem, with the onboarding decline plausibly upstream of the activation decline. Fixing the upstream constriction is the intervention most likely to compound, and memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value across self-serve) plus memory_31 (signup simplification producing a durable first-week activation lift) both support it. memory_91 (activation messaging) is real but treats a symptom further down the funnel; it remains the fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding story.

I spend the second pull on memory_86 because it is the memory I actually intend to act on — I want the original record's magnitude, duration, and segment definitions, not just the consolidated summary. Two specific risks I need it to speak to: whether the lift persisted past the first week or decayed, and whether 'self-serve accounts' included the enterprise-adjacent traffic that memory_44 says converts better through sales-assisted flows. If it did, aggressive simplification could route high-value prospects away from the demo path and trade pipeline quality for completion-rate cosmetics.

That last risk is the reason for standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout, and for holding the enterprise/demo path out of scope so the sales-assisted route stays intact. I am also treating 'completion' as an instrument, not the goal: removing required fields can raise completion while stripping the qualification and routing data that makes revenue qualified, so success criteria should be downstream qualified conversion and retention, with completion as a secondary read. Both supporting memories are consolidated summaries of records up to two months old, and neither was measured under current competitive pressure, so the effect size should be treated as directional rather than as a point estimate. referral_incentive (memory_57) is credible but addresses established customers, not the acquisition and activation gaps that are actually moving.
